SDF Rounding is a geometric transformation that rounds the edges of a shape by a specified radius [S1, unofficial][S2, unofficial].

The claim states that SDF Rounding is a geometric transformation that rounds the edges of a shape by a specified radius. Source [S1] explicitly defines it as 'A geometric transformation that rounds the edges of a shape by a specified radius' and notes that it involves subtracting the radius from the SDF value. Source [S2] confirms that rounding an SDF involves subtracting a constant distance value (the rounding radius) from the SDF result. Both sources support the definition and mechanism described in the claim.

It operates by subtracting a constant distance value from the SDF result [S2, unofficial], distinguishing it from [SDF Domain Manipulation Operators](1730-sdf-domain-manipulation-operators.md) which modify the coordinate space, and [SDF Primitives](1731-sdf-primitives.md) which define base shapes [S1, unofficial][S2, unofficial].

The claim states that the operation works by subtracting a constant distance value from the SDF result. Source [S2] explicitly notes 'Rounding an SDF by subtracting a constant distance value from the SDF result' and shows code `return self.sdf(query_coords).subtract(self.rounding)`. Source [S1] notes also state 'Subtract the radius r from the SDF value.' The claim distinguishes this from coordinate space modification (transformations) and base shape definition (primitives). Source [S2] imports `SDFOnion` (which corresponds to the rounding operation described) separately from `SDFAffineTransformation` (coordinate space modification) and `SDFSphere`, `SDFBox`, etc. (primitives). Source [S1] has a section 'Geometric Transformations' which includes `translation`, implying a distinction between transformations and the rounding operation described in the notes. Thus, all facts in the claim are supported by the evidence.
